issues.legal_issue: An appellate decree that supersedes a trial court decree is the operative decree for determining when the decree was passed.
material_facts: A preliminary decree was passed by the trial court before the debt-relief law came into force.
Appeals from that decree were pending when the debt-relief law came into force.

The appellate court later issued a preliminary decree that modified the relief granted to some defendants and affirmed the decree against the applicant, and a final decree was subsequently passed on that basis.
issues.conclusion: The trial court decrees were superseded, and the appellate preliminary decree, made final by the later final decree, was the operative decree.
issues.legal_principle: On appeal, the appellate decree becomes the operative decree and the decree below merges in it. The Court relied on Jowad Hussain v. Gendan Singh, which approved Gajadhar Singh v. Kishan Jiwan Lal on the effect of an appellate decree in mortgage proceedings, and on The Collector of Customs, Calcutta v. The East India Commercial Co. Ltd. for the principle that the appellate order is operative after the appeal is disposed of.

predicates.appeal_from_preliminary_mortgage_decree: The proceeding was an appeal from a preliminary decree in a mortgage suit.
predicates.appellate_court_issued_decree_supersedin: The appellate court issued a decree that replaced or modified the trial court decree.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a preliminary mortgage decree results in a decree replacing or modifying the trial court decree, the appellate decree is the operative decree.

issues.legal_issue: An unsatisfied decretal debt may be considered for statutory scaling where the operative decree falls within the debt-relief law as extended by the later amendment, subject to the debtor proving eligibility.
material_facts: The operative preliminary decree was made by the appellate court after the principal debt-relief law came into force, and a final decree followed.
The final decree had not been satisfied in full when the amending law came into force.
The applicant sought to scale down the decretal debt, but the court had not yet determined whether the applicant was an eligible agriculturist.
issues.conclusion: The applicant was entitled to have the scaling application considered under the amended law, provided he established that he was an agriculturist entitled to its benefit.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 19(2) and 16(iii) of the Madras Agriculturists Relief Act, 1938, as amended by Madras Act 23 of 1948, apply to a decree passed after the principal Act commenced where the decree remained unsatisfied in full when the amendment commenced. The word “debt” includes a decretal debt. The Court followed Narayanan Chettiar v. Annamalai Chettiar on the scope of clause (iii) and the meaning of debt.

rule.if: application_to_scale_decretal_debt and operative_decree_passed_after_relief_law_started and decree_not_fully_satisfied_at_amendment and debtor_is_eligible_agriculturist

predicates.application_to_scale_decretal_debt: The debtor applied for statutory scaling of a debt embodied in a decree.
predicates.operative_decree_passed_after_relief_law: The operative decree was passed after the debt-relief law had commenced.
predicates.decree_not_fully_satisfied_at_amendment: The decree had not been satisfied in full when the later amendment commenced.
predicates.debtor_is_eligible_agriculturist: The debtor is an agriculturist eligible for the debt-relief benefit.

issues.definition: A debtor may claim scaling relief when the debtor applies to scale a decretal debt, the operative decree was passed after the relief law began, the decree remained partly unsatisfied when the amendment began, and the debtor is an eligible agriculturist.

issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of an application made before a newly created statutory right arose does not bar a later claim to that right.
material_facts: The applicant’s earlier applications for relief under the principal law were rejected before the 1948 amendment created the right on which the later application relied.
The final decree remained unsatisfied in full when the amendment came into force.
The applicant then made a fresh application relying on the amended law.
issues.conclusion: The earlier dismissals did not bar the applicant from claiming the new right created by the amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 19(2) and 16(iii) of the Madras Agriculturists Relief Act, 1938, as amended by Madras Act 23 of 1948, created a new right in the circumstances described. The principle of res judicata could not defeat a right that had not existed when the earlier applications were dismissed; the Court also relied on Narayanan Chettiar v. Annamalai Chettiar in construing the amendment.

predicates.application_to_scale_decretal_debt: The debtor applied for statutory scaling of a debt embodied in a decree.
predicates.earlier_relief_claim_rejected_before_new: The debtor's earlier claim for relief was rejected before the later statutory right arose.

issues.definition: An earlier rejection does not bar a new claim when the debtor applies to scale a decretal debt and the earlier relief claim was rejected before the new right arose.
